This is a Walther TPH in 22 long rifle manufactured in the U.S. by Interarms. I tested it out today with four different ammunition brands. 3 worked reasonably well with some malfunctions (generally failure to eject), 1 brand failed to eject after every round and also had issues firing the first time. So the internet wisdom about needing high velocity ammunition seems to be true for the most part, unless you're willing to modify springs or whatever.

My overall impression about this gun is that it's well put together and is a very concealable weapon that you can carry when something else isn't practical. For example, if you're out in jeans and a t-shirt, and you've gained 30 lbs but don't want to admit it and move up a size or three, you can throw this in your pocket still not be obvious about carrying a weapon. It's light enough that you'll forget you're carrying something, but since it's not a polymer gun it has a heft to it that's reassuring.

I did experience some minor slide bite, but that's fixed by adjusting your grip. Overall I shoot this as well or better than my PPS M2 in 9mm and I can fire rounds much quicker due to the negligible recoil. I could probably shoot an entire magazine of 6 rounds and start reloading by the time I'd get off 3 or 4 well aimed shots with a 9mm. So while it's not powerful and isn't something you might want as a primary sidearm, it would be much better than walking around with nothing.
